vos.title: Fake AI Trading Bot Tutorials Drain 274.6 Ethereum (ETH) From 224 Victims, TRM Labs Finds
vos.subTitle:
• Fake YouTube tutorials promoting Claude AI arbitrage bots drained 274.6 ETH
• TRM Labs traced 234 malicious contracts deployed by 224 victims
• Stolen funds worth about $517,000 moved to six collection addresses
274.6 ETH Lost to Fake Claude Tutorials
A network of fake YouTube tutorials promising an automated arbitrage bot built with Anthropic’s Claude has drained 274.6 Ethereum (ETH), worth roughly $517,000, from 224 victims, according to a Sep. 14 report from blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. The operation stood out from conventional drainer campaigns because it never asked anyone to connect a wallet to a suspicious site or sign an unclear approval. Instead, victims followed step-by-step video instructions and deployed malicious smart contracts themselves, executing every transaction with their own approvals. TRM identified nine near-identical tutorials circulated under different creator identities, each fronted by AI-generated hosts and voiceovers that lent the videos the look of independent guides. Viewers were told to copy code and open a compiler website chosen by the presenter, some of which copied the design of Remix, the widely used browser-based environment for building Ethereum contracts. The firm traced 234 contracts deployed through the funnel; because several participants created more than one, the affected headcount came to 224. Once funded, the contracts forwarded balances to six collection addresses controlled by the operators, and TRM calculated a median loss of 1 ETH per incident — evidence that the take was distributed across many small victims rather than concentrated in one large deposit. Based on ETH’s price when the transfers settled, the aggregate haul reached approximately $517,000.
How the Hidden Drainer Code Worked
The deception sat one layer earlier than most phishing: at code generation. In the variant TRM examined, a backend script ignored whatever source the victim pasted into the compiler and instead retrieved a separate contract from a server the scammers controlled, preparing the replacement for deployment. The clean code displayed in the browser never reached the chain — users saw one program on screen while their wallets deployed another, so a visual check of the compiler window could not reveal the swap. The replacement contract accepted ETH deposits, matching the expected behavior of a trading bot that needed working capital. But once its balance exceeded 0.05 ETH, the contract was set to sweep the money to an operator-controlled address the moment the user pressed either the Start or Withdraw button. Both controls served the same drain function despite their legitimate-looking labels, and no AI model ever interacted with the deployed code — the Claude branding was purely part of the pitch. Because each victim initiated and approved the deployment, funding and function calls — paying their own gas fees at every step — the transaction trail looked nothing like a typical attack requesting a broad token allowance. Common wallet protections had little to flag: a fresh contract address would not appear on existing blocklists, and no seed phrase was ever surrendered.
Bytecode Verification Becomes the First Defense
Our reading of this campaign is that the attack surface has shifted from wallet approvals to the code-supply chain itself, and users deploying anything from a tutorial should verify the actual bytecode before funding it. Context matters: Ethereum security groups, including the Ethereum ecosystem’s Security Alliance network spanning MetaMask, Phantom, WalletConnect and Backpack, put 2025 drainer losses at $84 million — the lowest on record — and the Ethereum Foundation backed a dedicated engineer in February to disrupt such tooling. As tutorials grow more convincing, that downward trend faces a real test.

لم يأتِ هذا الصعود من فراغ، إذ ارتفعت الفائدة المفتوحة على عقود سولانا الآجلة بنسبة 18%، وهو مؤشر يراقبه المتداولون عن كثب لأنه يعكس حجم المراكز المفتوحة ومدى شهية المخاطرة في السوق.

vos.title: "Micron Rebounds 5.5% as Memory Tightness Returns to Focus, Taiwan Labor Talks Hit Key Date"
vos.subTitle:
Micron Technology shares jumped 5.5% to $977.50 on Thursday, putting the stock back above its pre-Monday level as tight memory supply returned to the center of the semiconductor trade.
The rebound now meets a company-specific labor test in Taiwan, where Friday is one of two key mediation dates, and unions have warned they could move toward a strike vote if Micron fails to produce a concrete profit-sharing proposal.
Micron Erases Monday’s AI-Slowdown Selloff
Micron fell 5.25% to $924.03 on Monday as calls from several AI-industry leaders for slower AI development pressured chipmakers. By Thursday’s close, the stock had climbed back to $977.50, about 0.2% above its Sept. 11 close of $975.26, effectively erasing the net loss from the week’s initial AI-slowdown shock, according to Micron’s historical closing prices. Reuters reported that the Monday decline came as AI-slowdown warnings broadly hit semiconductor shares.
Thursday’s move was not isolated. Intel gained 7.7%, AMD rose about 6.5%, and SanDisk advanced 6.2% during a broad semiconductor rebound, while falling oil prices and Treasury yields also supported the wider market. Micron also had a memory-specific tailwind after Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan warned that memory capacity remained constrained and supply pressure could persist into next year.
That supply backdrop matters because Micron’s recent earnings have been built on unusually strong memory pricing and margins. Micron’s fiscal third-quarter results showed revenue of $41.46 billion and a non-GAAP gross margin of 84.9%, followed by guidance for roughly $50 billion of fourth-quarter revenue and an approximately 86% gross margin.
Wall Street is also focused on how long the memory shortage can last. Goldman Sachs maintained a “Neutral” rating and $1,100 target on Sept. 11, expecting another strong quarter because of tight DRAM and NAND conditions while flagging longer-term supply additions, particularly from China. TD Cowen’s Krish Sankar, by contrast, reiterated a “Buy” rating and $1,600 target this week, arguing that Micron appears further along in margin expansion than in the underlying demand cycle. 
Taiwan Labor Dispute Puts Supply Risk Back in Focus
The same tight-supply story that helped Micron shares Thursday increases the significance of its Taiwan labor dispute. According to Reuters’ report on Micron’s Taiwan labor dispute, unions representing more than 80% of Micron’s roughly 15,000 Taiwan employees are seeking a permanent system allocating 15% of operating profit to employees. Union representatives said that if Micron does not present a concrete proposal during the Sept. 18 and Sept. 21 process, they could declare negotiations broken down and move toward a strike vote.
No strike had been called, and production had not been affected in Reuters’ latest confirmed report. Friday marks the Taichung union’s scheduled first mediation session, while further mediation involving the Taoyuan union is scheduled for Sept. 21. A Friday-morning status review found no confirmed strike announcement or production interruption.
Taiwan is nevertheless a critical Micron manufacturing center for DRAM and high-bandwidth memory, meaning an eventual work stoppage could matter more while memory supply is already constrained. Micron has said it remains committed to participating in mediation in good faith.
The dispute continued even after Micron announced fiscal-2026 rewards worth 35 to 68 months of pay for Taiwan direct labor employees. The union has argued that those awards are one-off compensation rather than the permanent, transparent profit-sharing structure it is seeking. Reuters detailed Micron’s Taiwan compensation package.
Tokenized Micron Market Remains Active
Separately, Micron’s tokenized counterpart remains active on Binance. Binance officially opened MUB/USDT Spot trading in June, establishing MUB as an active bStock linked to Micron.
At the latest check on Friday morning, Binance’s MUB/USDT Spot market showed MUB at $992.49.
MUB trades in a different market and measurement window from Micron’s Thursday 5.5% regular-session gain, so the figures should not be treated as directly equivalent. Binance states that MUB is a bStock issued by BTech Holdings representing an interest in underlying securities rather than direct ownership of Micron shares.
Micron’s next confirmed financial catalyst comes Sept. 30, when the company will hold its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call at 2:30 p.m. Mountain time. Micron confirmed the Sept. 30 earnings date in August.
Investor Takeaway
Micron’s 5.5% Thursday rally restored the stock to roughly its pre-Monday level as attention swung back from AI-spending concerns toward memory scarcity. The Taiwan dispute now tests that supply narrative from another direction, with the Sept. 18 and Sept. 21 mediation process preceding any potential strike vote and Micron’s Sept. 30 earnings providing the next confirmed financial update.

vos.title: Binance Withdraws Greek MiCA License Bid for Bitcoin (BTC) Services After Lagarde Intervention
vos.subTitle:
• Binance withdrew its Greek MiCA license application on June 24, before any formal decision was issued
• ECB President Christine Lagarde reportedly asked Greek PM Mitsotakis to block Binance's approval
• Greece's capital market commission had notified ESMA of its intent to approve Binance's application
Binance Pulls Greek Application June 24
Binance has withdrawn its application for a Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) license in Greece after European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde privately intervened to block its approval, according to a report published Sept. 18 by The Wall Street Journal. Lagarde is said to have personally asked Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis not to green-light the filing — a request that preceded Binance's decision to pull the application on June 24. The license would have allowed Binance to offer regulated crypto-asset services, including trading and custody of assets such as Bitcoin (BTC), across the entire bloc. As of the report's publication, neither Lagarde, the ECB nor the Greek authorities involved had confirmed or denied the account, and Binance has made no public statement addressing the reported intervention.
The application had been moving toward approval. The Hellenic Capital Market Commission, the national regulator reviewing the file, had determined that Binance's documentation was complete and, following MiCA procedure, notified the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) of its intent to approve. The turn came in early June, when the commission informed Binance that Lagarde had voiced her opposition directly to the Greek prime minister. Binance then withdrew on June 24, which meant the commission's board never had to issue a formal rejection. The only objectively verifiable fact remains the withdrawal itself — Binance holds no MiCA license from any EU member state. The report attributed two concerns to Lagarde: Binance's guilty-plea record in the United States, and the expansion of dollar-denominated stablecoins, whose tokenomics could undercut the ECB's digital euro project and euro-denominated alternatives. What makes the episode notable is jurisdiction. Under ESMA's MiCA framework, licensing authority sits with each member state's national regulator, and a license granted in any single state passports the holder EU-wide — the ECB holds no formal approval or veto role. What the reporting describes, then, is not a central bank exercising statutory power but its president working through political channels to influence a member-state government.
Banks Double on ESMA Register
As one crypto-native incumbent exits the EU's licensing track, traditional banks are racing onto the same register. The number of banks listed as crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) under MiCA doubled to about 80 from roughly 40 between June 26 and Sept. 16, based on ESMA's official register data. Over the same period, the total count of listed CASPs climbed from 243 to 349 — but non-bank providers lost relative ground, their share slipping from about 84% to 77%, while banks lifted theirs from around 17% to nearly 23%. The profile of Europe's regulated crypto market is visibly shifting toward incumbent finance.
Germany accounts for much of the banking influx. Dozens of cooperative and commercial lenders appear on the register, including institutions from the Volksbank, Raiffeisenbank and VR Bank networks — evidence that regulated crypto services are reaching regional banking, not just global groups. Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest lender, announced plans on Wednesday to launch digital asset custody for institutional and corporate clients in Europe, with a spokesperson indicating the bank expects MiCA regulatory approval for the offering in October. Institutional custody of this kind is a different proposition from the self-custody model retail users manage with hardware devices and a Ledger Recovery Key; banks are building the custodial rails that funds and corporates require. The speed of the expansion owes to a structural shortcut: where crypto companies must complete full CASP authorization, credit institutions can offer crypto-asset services — custody, trading and execution across spot and derivatives such as crypto options — through a lighter notification route. Article 60 of MiCA permits a credit institution to provide these services provided it submits the required information to its home regulator at least 40 working days before offering them for the first time. Lenders already distributing conventional instruments like the S&P 500 ETF can therefore enter crypto without a bespoke licensing process.
MiCA Passport Becomes the Prize
Taken together, the two threads sketch a European market at an inflection point. The register's own composition shows who is winning access: the framework ESMA administers is being absorbed fastest by incumbent banks using the Article 60 notification route, while the industry's most heavily used exchange was reportedly squeezed out through channels outside the rulebook. Our reading at COINOTAG is that the MiCA passport is now the decisive asset in Europe — and who obtains it is being settled as much by politics as by the authorization files themselves.

vos.subTitle:
انتشرت مؤخراً مقاطع تعليمية مزيفة تزعم أنها تشرح كيفية بناء روبوتات تداول تعمل بالذكاء الاصطناعي، لكنها في الحقيقة فخ محكم استهدف مستخدمي العملات الرقمية. وبحسب ما تم رصده، فقد وقع 224 شخصاً في هذا الفخ وخسروا ما مجموعه 274.6 من عملة $ETH.

تعتمد الحيلة على إيهام الضحايا بأنهم يتعلمون إنشاء بوت تداول ذكي، لكن ما يحدث فعلياً هو دفعهم إلى نشر عقود ذكية خبيثة على الشبكة. وبمجرد تنفيذ هذه العقود، يتم تحويل الأموال من محافظ الضحايا إلى محافظ المهاجمين دون أن يدركوا ما يجري.

تقدر القيمة السوقية للأموال المسروقة بنحو 517 ألف دولار، وهو مبلغ كبير يعكس حجم الضحايا الذين انخدعوا بهذه المقاطع. وتشير المعطيات إلى أن العملية لم تكن فردية، بل استهدفت عدداً كبيراً من المستخدمين بشكل منظم.

ما زال من غير الواضح حتى الآن ما إذا كانت هناك جهات تحقق في هذه الحادثة أو ما إذا كان قد تم تحديد هوية الجناة. كما لم تصدر أي جهة رسمية بياناً حول ما إذا كان يمكن استرداد الأموال المسروقة أم لا.

القصة تسلط الضوء على مخاطر الثقة العمياء في المحتوى التعليمي المنتشر على منصات الفيديو، خصوصاً عندما يتعلق الأمر بنشر عقود ذكية أو التعامل مع أدوات تداول آلية. وينصح الخبراء بالتحقق من أي كود قبل تنفيذه وعدم منح صلاحيات غير محدودة للمحافظ.

Recently, fake educational clips claiming to explain how to build AI-powered trading robots have spread, but in reality they are a well-crafted trap targeting cryptocurrency users. According to what has been observed, 224 people have fallen for this trap and lost a total of 274.6 in $ETH.

The scam relies on making victims believe they are learning to create a smart trading bot, but what actually happens is that they are prompted to publish malicious smart contracts on the network. Once these contracts are executed, funds are transferred from the victims’ wallets to the attackers’ wallets without the victims realizing what is going on.

vos.title: EU Banks on MiCA Registry Double to 80, Widening Bitcoin (BTC) Access
vos.subTitle:
• Banks on the EU MiCA CASP registry doubled from about 40 to 80 by September 16.
• Total authorized CASPs grew from 243 to 349 over the same period.
• Bank share of the CASP register rose from 17% to 23%.
From 40 Banks to 80
The register of firms authorized to serve Europe's crypto market under MiCA used to read almost entirely like a startup directory — specialist brokers, custodians and trading venues built for digital assets from day one. That composition is shifting toward institutions, and the shift is now measurable. Registry data shows the number of banks listed as crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets framework doubled from roughly 40 to 80 between June 26 and September 16, according to Coinreaders. Over the same window, the total count of authorized CASPs climbed from 243 to 349, which means new bank entrants took a disproportionate slice of every registration added across the summer. The share math makes the tilt explicit: banks held 17% of the register in late June and 23% by mid-September, while non-bank providers — the firms that defined the first phase of Europe's licensed market — slipped from roughly 84% to 77%. All figures reflect the September 16 snapshot of the register. A CASP authorization is the umbrella license MiCA created for custody, exchange operation, execution and advice: a firm that secures it in one member state can passport those services across the entire bloc. The dynamic tracks the framework's maturation rather than a single quarter's anomaly. As MiCA's authorization regime settles into routine operation, the onboarding queue is no longer dominated by crypto-native applicants racing the compliance deadline. Licensed banks that spent the framework's early months observing from the sidelines are filing in steadily increasing numbers, and each approval converts a traditional institution into a regulated gateway for Bitcoin (BTC) and the wider token market inside the European Union. For a framework whose early skeptics doubted legacy finance would bother applying at all, the register now supplies a clear empirical answer: the banks are applying, the pace is accelerating, and the institutional share of Europe's licensed crypto infrastructure rises with every reporting cycle.
What a CASP License Buys a Bank
The June-to-September window captures MiCA's first full quarter of steady-state operation, which is what makes the doubling of bank registrations more than a bookkeeping curiosity. For the institutions, the filing calculus is straightforward: a CASP license obtained from one national competent authority unlocks a passport across all 27 member states, letting a bank extend an existing deposit and brokerage relationship into digital assets without erecting a fresh legal entity per country. In practical terms, that means a retail client can be offered token custody, spot execution and — where the underlying networks permit — staking on proof-of-stake chains under the same regulated roof as familiar savings products. The competitive pressure lands on the specialist venues that built Europe's licensed retail market. Firms whose platforms were engineered around granular candlestick trading of tokens issued via smart contracts now compete with banks delivering equivalent regulated services inside apps customers already open every day — a distribution advantage the crypto-native sector spent years assembling along the Robinhood-style retail brokerage model. The framework's effect on established European trading venues is one of licensing-parity pressure rather than displacement: the specialists keep their head start, but the moat narrows with each bank approval, and the contrast sharpens when licensed local providers are set against the best crypto exchanges globally. What carries over untouched is scale. With 349 authorized CASPs as of September 16, non-bank firms still outnumber bank registrants roughly three to one and hold 77% of the register. The institutional acceleration widens the market's regulated perimeter; it has not yet rewritten its leadership. The direction, though, is unambiguous: every reporting window since late June has added banks to the list, the share arithmetic moved roughly six points in a single summer, and the reading around the data is uniform — with MiCA's regime in place, the pace of European banks' entry into crypto is picking up cycle by cycle.
The 77% Non-Bank Majority
The legal footing for all of it is Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 — MiCA itself — whose CASP title has bound every firm offering crypto-asset services in the Union since December 30, 2024, with the stablecoin provisions applying six months earlier. The rule text requires authorization from a home-state national competent authority before any such services may be offered; the doubling of bank entries is that requirement operating as designed, filtering applicants into a single, passportable license. What it does not change is who holds most of the register: with non-bank firms still at 77%, Europe's specialist crypto layer remains the majority — for now — even as the institutional share climbs.

vos.title: Can You Buy U.S. Stocks Through a Crypto Exchange in Ethiopia?
vos.subTitle:
Yes, eligible users in Ethiopia can buy and sell more than 7,000 U.S.-listed stocks and ETFs through Binance using supported crypto balances. Binance Stocks Trading is provided through Nest Trading Limited, which routes securities orders to Alpaca Securities LLC for execution, clearing, settlement and custody. Availability depends on the user's jurisdiction, account status and eligibility.
For crypto users, this creates a different way to access traditional markets: instead of moving crypto to a separate brokerage, eligible users can access U.S. stocks and ETFs through the Binance ecosystem.
The important distinction is that Binance Direct Stocks and Binance bStocks are two different products. Direct Stocks give eligible users beneficial ownership of the securities they purchase, while bStocks are blockchain-based tokenized securities backed 1:1 by underlying securities but do not represent direct ownership of the underlying shares.

Can You Buy U.S. Stocks on Binance in Ethiopia?
For eligible Ethiopian users, Binance provides access to its U.S. Stocks & ETFs trading service.
Binance currently advertises more than 7,000 listed stocks and ETFs, with investments starting from as little as $5. Selected stocks also support fractional investing, allowing users to buy less than one whole share.
This means an eligible user does not necessarily need to open a separate traditional brokerage account to gain access to the supported U.S. securities through Binance.
However, availability should always be checked inside the user's Binance account. Binance states that securities products may not be available in every region, and eligibility can depend on jurisdiction and applicable requirements.
For Ethiopian users, this distinction is important: being able to access Binance itself does not automatically mean every Binance financial product is available to every user.

How Does Stock Trading on Binance Work?
Binance Stocks Trading is provided by Nest Trading Limited and operates in cooperation with an external brokerage. For securities transactions, Nest Trading acts as the introducing broker and routes orders to Alpaca Securities LLC, which handles execution, clearing, settlement and custody. Binance does not itself handle or custody the securities.
The user experience, however, remains inside Binance.
Stock purchases are primarily made using USDC. Binance also supports certain other assets, including USDT and BNB, which can be automatically converted to USDC when an eligible stock order is submitted. The assets used for the purchase need to be held in the Funding or Spot Account.
For example, an eligible user holding USDT does not necessarily need to manually sell the USDT for USDC first. Binance can handle the supported conversion as part of the stock-order process.
When a stock is sold, the proceeds are credited as USDC to the user's Funding Account.
Binance currently describes stock trading as supporting different trading sessions depending on the security, including Regular, Extended and 24-hour sessions. Market orders are available during Regular Trading Hours, generally 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

Which U.S. Stocks and ETFs Can You Trade on Binance?
Binance currently advertises access to more than 7,000 listed stocks and ETFs.
The selection covers companies and funds across different sectors and market segments. The Binance Stocks page currently highlights names including:
AppleMicrosoftNVIDIAAlphabetAmazonMetaTeslaNetflixAMDJPMorganVisaMastercard
The exact securities available to an individual user can depend on product availability and eligibility.
The platform also supports fractional shares for selected stocks, meaning users do not always need enough capital to purchase an entire share. Binance says the minimum investment can start at $5.
This can be particularly relevant when a single share of a company has a high market price: instead of buying one complete share, an eligible user can purchase a fraction.

Which U.S. Stocks Can You Trade Through Binance?
The answer is broader than simply a handful of large technology companies.
Binance's current offering includes 7,000+ listed stocks and ETFs, giving eligible users access to securities across multiple sectors and categories. That can include large-cap companies, smaller companies and ETFs, depending on what is supported by the brokerage infrastructure and available to the user's account.
The important point is that Binance's stock product is not simply a collection of tokenized versions of a few famous companies.
Direct Stocks are actual securities exposure through the brokerage structure, with the user identified as the beneficial owner of the shares they purchase. That is fundamentally different from buying a crypto token that merely tracks the price of a stock.

Can You Buy Binance bStocks in Ethiopia?
bStocks require a separate explanation.
bStocks are tokenized securities issued by BTech Holdings Limited, a Binance group affiliate. Each bStock is backed 1:1 by a corresponding U.S. share held with a regulated custodian. However, owning a bStock is not the same thing as directly owning the underlying U.S. share.
bStocks are structured as certificates representing interests in underlying securities. They can trade on Binance's spot market and, where permitted, can be withdrawn to a compatible BNB Smart Chain wallet.
There is an important geographic limitation.
Binance currently states that bStocks are not available in all jurisdictions and are offered only to eligible users in permitted jurisdictions on a secondary-market basis. Binance also provides a country-eligibility mechanism for determining whether a jurisdiction qualifies. Therefore, it would be inaccurate to state that every Ethiopian Binance user automatically has access to bStocks.
For an Ethiopian user, the practical check is whether bStocks appear as an available product in the Binance account and whether the account passes the applicable eligibility requirements.
This is also why Binance Stocks and Binance bStocks should not be treated as interchangeable products.

The distinction is important because the two products serve different purposes.

Relevant FAQs
Are Binance bStocks available in Ethiopia?
bStocks are subject to geographic eligibility and are not available in every jurisdiction. Binance's current terms state that bStocks are offered only to eligible users in permitted jurisdictions on a secondary-market basis. Users should check their Binance account and the current eligibility requirements rather than assuming availability based solely on country.
Are bStocks the same as U.S. shares?
No.
A bStock is a tokenized security backed 1:1 by an underlying U.S. share, but it does not give the holder direct ownership of that underlying share. Binance describes bStocks as certificates representing interests in the underlying securities.
By contrast, Binance's Direct Stocks product identifies the user as the beneficial owner of the shares purchased through the securities-trading service.
Can you buy U.S. stocks on Binance using USDT?
Yes, for eligible users.
Binance's current Stocks Trading documentation says stock purchases are primarily made using USDC, while supported assets including USDT and BNB can be automatically converted to USDC when the stock order is submitted.
So a user holding USDT can potentially fund a stock purchase without first manually transferring funds to a separate brokerage.
Can you buy U.S. stocks on Binance from Ethiopia?
Eligible users in Ethiopia can access Binance's Stocks & ETFs product, subject to the applicable account, product and jurisdictional requirements.
The available securities and services can change, so users should check the Stocks section of their Binance account before trading. Binance currently advertises more than 7,000 listed stocks and ETFs and a minimum investment starting at $5.
What is the difference between buying a stock and buying a bStock?
Buying a stock through Binance's Direct Stocks service gives the user beneficial ownership of the purchased security through the brokerage structure.
Buying a bStock instead provides exposure through a tokenized security backed 1:1 by the underlying share. The bStock itself is not direct ownership of that share.
For crypto-native users, bStocks additionally bring blockchain features such as 24/7 trading and the ability, where permitted, to withdraw the token to a compatible BNB Smart Chain wallet.
The Bigger Shift: From Crypto Exchange to Multi-Asset Platform
For Ethiopian crypto users, the significance of Binance's stock offering goes beyond simply adding another asset category.
A user can hold crypto, stablecoins and other digital assets while also accessing U.S. stocks and ETFs through the same broader ecosystem, subject to eligibility.
That does not make Binance a replacement for every traditional brokerage. Different platforms have different products, jurisdictions, fees and legal structures.
But the direction is clear: the boundary between a crypto exchange and a broader investment platform is becoming less distinct.
For users in markets where international investment access can be difficult, the ability to move between supported crypto balances and U.S. securities within one platform represents a meaningful change in how those markets can be accessed.
The key is understanding what you are actually buying.
Direct Stocks, bStocks and crypto assets may all appear within the same Binance ecosystem, but they have different legal structures, ownership rights, settlement mechanisms and geographic restrictions.
That distinction matters just as much as the number of assets available.

vos.title: Evernorth Lands $30 Million Convertible Note to Fuel XRP (XRP) Treasury
vos.subTitle:
• Evernorth secured a $30 million convertible-note commitment from NH Investment & Securities.
• Evernorth plans to spend the full $30 million buying spot XRP on the open market.
• Evernorth targets a Nasdaq listing under the ticker XRPN after its SPAC merger.
Evernorth Secures $30 Million Commitment
Evernorth, positioned as the world's largest XRP treasury vehicle, has locked in a $30 million convertible-note commitment from NH Investment & Securities, one of South Korea's foremost investment institutions. The commitment was publicized through a Whale Insider update posted on X, and it lands at a moment when institutional accumulation of the Ripple-linked asset is visibly accelerating. Convertible notes are debt instruments that can later convert into equity, which means the Korean backer effectively funds Evernorth's token accumulation today while holding a claim on the company's future shares. The deployment plan is unusually direct: the entire $30 million is earmarked for purchasing spot XRP on the open market, with no portion reserved for operating costs or debt service, according to the commitment terms disclosed so far. That structure makes the raise a near-immediate source of open-market demand, and desk watchers of spot trading volume will be looking for its footprint as executions begin. The timing also matters. Treasury-style accumulation has become one of the defining demand narratives for the asset this cycle, and a top-of-category buyer adding fresh, fully allocated capital reinforces that bid at a point when retail flows have been choppy. Related whale positioning has been notable as well — recent reporting tracked XRP whales sending 1.6 billion tokens to Binance in the largest such movement since March — underscoring how concentrated holders are repositioning while treasury firms step up their buying.
SPAC Merger and Nasdaq Listing Path
The financing is embedded in a broader corporate objective: Evernorth's ongoing merger with a special purpose acquisition company. A SPAC is a publicly traded shell company created specifically to take a private firm public without a conventional IPO, and completing that merger is the intended stepping stone to Evernorth listing on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN. Once listed, the company plans to give traditional investors equity-market exposure to an XRP-focused corporate treasury strategy — participation in the asset's upside without directly buying tokens or managing a crypto wallet themselves. This mirrors the template popularized by Bitcoin and Ether treasury vehicles, but applies it to the XRP ecosystem, where public-market proxies have been scarcer. The two uses of the capital are explicitly linked in the company's plan: the raise both expands the treasury balance ahead of the public debut and supports the merger process that enables the debut. For NH Investment & Securities, the deal extends Korean institutional capital further into digital-asset infrastructure — a market where the country's exchanges already rank among the world's most active, as seen when JPYC volume overtook XRP on Upbit earlier this cycle. Investors tracking the ticker should note that a Nasdaq listing remains contingent on the merger closing; for those still deciding where to acquire the token directly, our beginner's guide to buying XRP covers the practical steps.
In COINOTAG's read, the official funding announcement is the load-bearing document here: it specifies a $30 million convertible-note commitment, names NH Investment & Securities as the backer, and binds the proceeds entirely to open-market spot purchases — while leaving the round's valuation and any wider investor syndicate undisclosed, a gap we flag rather than infer around. The thematic arc is consolidation: capital is migrating from scattered retail buying into structured, listed treasury vehicles, and Evernorth's SPAC-to-Nasdaq route would hand XRP its most prominent equity-market proxy to date. If the merger closes on schedule, XRPN becomes a new, observable channel for traditional flows into the asset — one worth monitoring alongside on-chain accumulation metrics going forward.

vos.title: تحذير أوروبي: الإشراف المركزي على MiCA قد يثقل كاهل شركات الكريبتو
vos.subTitle:
ظهر تحذير جديد من مسؤول في الجهة الرقابية الألمانية BaFin مفاده أن الإشراف المركزي على تنظيم الأسواق في الأصول المشفرة (MiCA) قد يفرض أعباء إضافية على شركات الكريبتو العاملة في أوروبا، في وقت تدرس فيه دول الاتحاد الأوروبي إصلاحات تتعلق بالقانون الخاص والتسويات. $BTC

ويأتي هذا التحذير وسط نقاش أوسع داخل الاتحاد الأوروبي حول كيفية تطبيق الإطار التنظيمي الموحد، وما إذا كان تركيز الإشراف في جهة مركزية واحدة سيؤدي إلى تعقيد الإجراءات على الشركات بدلاً من تبسيطها.

تشير الملاحظات إلى أن المراجعة الحالية لا تقتصر على قواعد الترخيص، بل تمتد إلى إصلاحات في القانون الخاص وآليات التسوية، وهي ملفات حساسة تؤثر مباشرة على طريقة عمل المنصات ومقدمي خدمات الأصول الرقمية.

ولم تصدر حتى الآن تفاصيل رسمية كاملة حول شكل الإصلاحات المقترحة أو الجدول الزمني لتنفيذها، ما يترك مجالاً لتأويلات متباينة حول مدى تأثيرها الفعلي على السوق الأوروبية.

في هذا السياق، يبقى المستثمرون والمشغلون في انتظار توضيحات إضافية من الجهات التنظيمية الأوروبية، خاصة أن أي تغيير في بنية الإشراف قد ينعكس على تكاليف الامتثال وسرعة الحصول على التراخيص.

translatedData.title: European warning: Central oversight of MiCA could burden crypto companies
translatedData.subTitle:
A new warning has been issued by an official at Germany’s regulatory authority BaFin, stating that central oversight of market regulation under MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets) could impose additional burdens on crypto companies operating in Europe, as EU member states consider reforms related to private law and settlements. $BTC

This warning comes amid a broader discussion within the European Union about how to implement the single regulatory framework, and whether concentrating supervision in a single central body would complicate procedures for firms instead of simplifying them.

vos.title: ناسا تختار سبيس إكس لإطلاق قمر ستاربست في 2028 وسط ترقب لمؤشر ناسداك
vos.subTitle:
أعلنت ناسا اختيار شركة سبيس إكس لإطلاق قمرها الصناعي ستاربست في عام 2028، في خطوة تعزز مكانة الشركة في قطاع الإطلاق الفضائي. ورغم هذا الاختيار، تراجع سهم سبيس إكس بنسبة 2% ليصل إلى 151.50 دولار، ما يثير تساؤلات حول انفصال أداء السهم عن الأخبار التشغيلية الإيجابية. $BTC

يأتي هذا التراجع في وقت يترقب فيه المستثمرون احتمال زيادة وزن السهم في مؤشر ناسداك-100، وهو حدث قد يجذب تدفقات من الصناديق المتداولة التي تتبع المؤشر. ويعد الانضمام بوزن أكبر إلى المؤشر محفزاً محتملاً للطلب على السهم.

حتى الآن، لا توجد تفاصيل رسمية مؤكدة حول توقيت أو حجم أي تعديل في أوزان المؤشر، ما يجعل الترقب سيد الموقف. كما لم تصدر سبيس إكس أو ناسداك أي تعليق إضافي بشأن الصفقة أو تأثيرها المالي.

يبقى السؤال الأهم: هل يعكس تراجع السهم اليوم مجرد جني أرباح مؤقت، أم أن السوق ينتظر تأكيدات ملموسة حول صفقة ناسا وتأثيرها على الإيرادات المستقبلية؟ الأيام المقبلة قد تحمل إجابة أوضح.

translatedData.title: NASA Selects SpaceX to Launch the Starbust Satellite in 2028 Amid Anticipation for the Nasdaq Index
translatedData.subTitle:
NASA announced its selection of SpaceX to launch its Starbust satellite in 2028, a move that strengthens the company’s position in the space launch sector. Despite this choice, SpaceX’s stock fell by 2% to $151.50, raising questions about the disconnect between the stock’s performance and positive operational news. $BTC

This decline comes as investors await the possibility of increasing the stock’s weighting in the Nasdaq-100 index, an event that could attract inflows from exchange-traded funds that track the index. A larger index weighting could be a potential catalyst for demand for the stock.
